bcrypt_verdict.english: What bcrypt says about `password` against a stored `hash`: Some(true) when it is the password the hash was made from, Some(false) when it is not, None when bcrypt cannot read the hash. Left abstract: its meaning is bcrypt's, taken on trust through `check_password`.

check_password.english: Asks bcrypt whether `password` matches the stored `hash`. Trusted, not proved: Verus cannot check bcrypt's hashing, so this wrapper's contract is assumed. Every password promise of `login_flow` rests on it.

check_password::2119b3d0a0aafc14e064633a.english: Its answer is its verdict: true for the right password, false for any other.

check_password::c1ace18c1f983a194e951d7f.english: bcrypt answers (Ok) exactly when it can read the stored hash.

No promise that the future completes.

login_flow.english: The whole login, awaited end to end: from the request's fields to the token or the HTTP error. Promises, on the awaited result: a token only for the account the login names and only with its right password, and always with it unless the lookup or signing fails with 500; the token carries that account's id and its table's role; refusals give today's 400, 401 or 500 and no token. Reads accounts and tokens through the abstract views above. No promise the future completes.
